subject: ClearWave - implementation steps for no-train & prompt/response ownership
body:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@clearwavehealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Green <sam.green@clearwavehealth.com>, Phil Adams <phil.adams@legalpartners.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Implementation questions for no-train & output ownership (next steps)

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the call today — helpful to understand Redwood's serving options. Before we sign the DPA addendum we have a couple of narrow implementation questions from procurement and legal that affect our rollout plan:

1) Operational evidence for the "no-training" commitment: what artifacts can Redwood provide to show customer traffic is excluded from model improvement (live runtime flags, E2E logs, or attestation)? Our security team needs a concrete list and an approximate delivery timeline.

2) Prompt/response ownership: we want the contract language to clearly state our customers retain IP to prompts and generated responses. Practically, what export controls or tooling will you provide so our product team can export conversation transcripts on-demand?

3) Subprocessors & geo-routing: can you confirm where the KV cache and ephemeral logs live for US-hosted Dedicated deployments? We need an explicit subprocessor list for our internal audit.

We'd like to close these in the next two weeks. Phil (external counsel) will prepare markups, but it helps if you can outline the operational steps we can point legal at.

Best,
Maya
Maya Singh
Procurement Manager, ClearWave Health
maya.singh@clearwavehealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

-----------------------------

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@clearwavehealth.com>
Cc: Sam Green <sam.green@clearwavehealth.com>, Phil Adams <phil.adams@legalpartners.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Implementation questions for no-train & output ownership (next steps)

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Below is a pragmatic implementation plan plus what we can provide as evidence. Looping in Lauren (Customer Success) for onboarding steps and Kimberly (Privacy & Legal ops) for the subprocessor and attestation items. Dev is cc'd for a short note about runtime flags.

High-level (timeline in parentheses):
- Evidence for no-train (2–4 business days):
  - Runtime flag confirmation: we can provide a signed statement plus a screenshot of the runtime config for your Dedicated pool showing learning=false.
  - Audit logs: delivery of an export (CSV) showing token routing and retention TTLs for a 30-day window.
  - Attestation: Redwood can provide a standard SOC2-style attestation letter specific to the "no-training" setting for customer traffic.

- Prompt/response ownership tooling (5–7 business days):
  - Conversation export API: we will enable an export endpoint scoped to your org for transcript pulls (JSON/CSV).
  - Downloadable transcript package: sample package (obfuscated PHI handled per your guidance) and instructions.

- Subprocessors & geo-routing (1–2 business days):
  - We'll supply a current subprocessor register and a mapping that shows which services touch ephemeral logs/KV cache for your Dedicated cluster. For US Dedicated the KV-cache & ephemeral logs are retained in the primary region (us-west-2) and handled by Redwood-managed services; we will list third-party subprocessors and whether they are used for backups, monitoring, or telemetry.

Attachments I'm sending with this note:
- redwood-no-train-implementation-checklist.pdf (detailed steps + artifacts)
- redwood-subprocessor-declaration-2026-12.pdf (current list)

Next steps: Phil — if you can share markups, Kimberly and I will review and aim to supply the attestation and exports by EOD next Thursday. Maya — can you confirm the export format you prefer (CSV vs JSON) and whether we should include full timestamps in UTC?

Thanks,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0204

-----------------------------

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Phil Adams <phil.adams@legalpartners.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@clearwavehealth.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Implementation questions for no-train & output ownership (next steps)

Phil / Maya — quick items from privacy/ops perspective:

1) Attestation language: we can provide a one-page attestation certifying that for your Dedicated cluster Redwood will not use customer payloads for model training or tuning. We cannot attest to downstream model behavior for non-customer-owned public models (we will call that out explicitly).

2) Subprocessor mapping: attached declaration enumerates subprocessors and categorizes them (hosting, monitoring, backups). If you need onshore-only processing we can discuss a limited subprocessor set for an onshore-only Dedicated pool (additional cost applies).

3) Export payloads: CSV is fine for procurement/audit; product teams often prefer JSON for nested conversation metadata. We will include UTC timestamps by default and an export-id (so you can correlate with our audit logs).

Dev — runtime flag detail for Maya: can you confirm the config path and a sample of the runtime flag name used so Maya's engineers can validate after we provide the screenshot?

Kimberly Park
Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

-----------------------------

From: Phil Adams <phil.adams@legalpartners.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@clearwavehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Implementation questions for no-train & output ownership (next steps)

Thanks Kimberly / team — that helps. A few minor asks from ClearWave legal:

- Please include a sample runtime-config screenshot (redacted UI ok) showing the learning toggle set to off and the cluster identifier so we can cross-check with the live instance after onboarding.
- We will accept the one-page attestation but request a clause that the attestation is refreshed annually or on request (standard).
- For the subprocessor list, please flag any subprocessors that could access unredacted transcripts (monitoring/logging partners) vs those that only process telemetry.

If you can upload the checklist and declaration to the Drive link and send a DocuSign addendum for the one-page attestation we can route internally and aim to sign next week.

Phil Adams
Counsel, LegalPartners (outside counsel to ClearWave)
phil.adams@legalpartners.com


[Attachments referenced above: redwood-no-train-implementation-checklist.pdf (PDF, 8 pages) | redwood-subprocessor-declaration-2026-12.pdf (PDF, 3 pages) | clearwave-dataflow-diagram.png (PNG, 1 file)]
